messages:
maria gonzalez: Brain dump: switch prefix ownership from continuous leases to a manifest-driven epoch CAS. Goal: reduce heartbeat pressure on hot prefixes and simplify hot-path ownership checks. Thoughts?

sam nguyen: Love to drop steady-state RPCs, but ownership semantics are trickier. How do we avoid two nodes serving the same prefix during topology changes?

maria gonzalez: Manifest is the single source of truth. Claim = CAS(manifest_id, old_blob, new_blob) where blob contains {epoch, owner, seq, tombstone_ts}. After CAS commits the new owner serves only when local_epoch == manifest_epoch.

linh tran: Nice. Q: in-flight requests from old owner that commit just before manifest flip—how are those reconciled?

maria gonzalez: Writes carry epoch+seq. New owner rejects writes with epoch < manifest_epoch. For ordering, we either drain a short window (best-effort) or require WAL replay from old owner. If drain fails, fallback to lease path for that prefix during migration window.

rahul: We'll need contested_count, claim_latency, epoch_flip_rate metrics and an alert on any dual-serve detection. I'll add hooks in the runtime to emit manifest_epoch with responses.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary started for manifest-epoch-proto on pool-canary-5. Monitor coord-store op rate: https://ci.internal/reports/3758

sam nguyen: What about split/merge? Multi-key CAS is painful. Suggest packing affected ranges into one manifest_blob so split/merge can be atomic without distributed transactions.

linh tran: Also GC: tombstones and monotonic epoch counters per-prefix. Never reuse epoch numbers. Compaction job trims history.

maria gonzalez: Migration plan sketch: feature flag manifests for read gating first (eviction unaffected), measure ops, then flip write gating behind operator guard + fallback to leases. CLI: rw-manifest describe/force-roll/revert.

rahul: Tests: CAS race unit test, chaos: owner crash during CAS, net partition between node and coord store, split/merge flapping. Harness will assert "no two nodes accept new writes for same prefix at overlapping times".

sam nguyen: Also ensure we don't degrade eviction heuristics. Keep eviction scoring local; manifest only gates serving.

linh tran: Client behavior: include observed_epoch in requests; server returns 409-like response when mismatch so clients refresh. Add soft-ttl on cached entries to reduce immediate inconsistency.

maria gonzalez: In RFC I'll state invariant explicitly: "After manifest commit at time t, at most one node may accept new write traffic for prefix P at epoch E." We'll include diagrams for handoff, split, merge, crash.

rahul: Ops telemetry + an operator emergency rollback command are must-haves. I'll prototype metrics and alerts.

maria gonzalez: OK I'll draft the RFC today. Aim to canary a minimal implementation in two sprints if approved.

sam nguyen: sgtm. Thanks everyone.

linh tran: :thumbsup:
